source_title: GLO original survey township plat, T. XVIII S. - R. XXXV E., East Florida (Tallahassee Meridian)
author: Henry Washington, Deputy Surveyor; approved V. Y. Conway, Surveyor General

where.url: https://glorecords.blm.gov/s/ (GLO Records portal; image via glo-entry-prod.blm.gov/ui/func/dsto/api/image/pdf/survey/<documentID>/... with the portal's public token)
where.id: BLM GLO Survey-12389; documentID 6951171212356315468; plat accession FL290180S0350E00001

caption_or_quote: Small hachured ring symbol labelled 'Turtle Mound' on the barrier strip between 'Eastern Channel' and the 'ATLANTIC OCEAN'; notes 'Surveyed in the 4th quarter of the year 1844 By Henry Washington D.S.'; 'Examined compared with the field notes and Approved March 20th 1845' (signed V. Y. Conway)
shows: Turtle Mound drawn as a hachured mound symbol and named; ocean shoreline, lagoon/'Eastern Channel' shore, the 'Islands and Marshes' of Mosquito Lagoon, Hillsboro River, sections 19/30/31 on the west margin, a road, 'White House' landmark. Scale 40 chains to an inch.
licence_basis: US federal government work (General Land Office, 1844-45): public domain
notes: Viewed full plat and zoomed crop. Only a symbol, not a plan of the mound's shape; useful as a georeferenced locator since shoreline and section lines are drawn. Same township also has a Diagram (Survey-59675, D. H. Burr) and resurveys (Survey-12391/12393) - not inspected for the mound.

source_title: GLO plat: Part of Township No. 46 South, Range No. 24 East of the Principal Meridian, Florida (survey of 'Key Mount' island, Sec. 36)
author: William E. Loper (surveyor, 1889); US Surveyor General's Office, Tallahassee

where.id: BLM GLO Survey-15187; documentID 13255526012196807251; plat accession FL290460S0240E00004

caption_or_quote: Island labelled 'KEY MOUNT' in Sec. 36 with lots 1-4 (25.27, 30.75, 27.65, 34.57 ac); in lot 4 a hachured symbol labelled 'Mound'; table 'Meanders of KEY MOUNT in Sec 36'; stamped 'RECEIVED WITH SUR. GENL'S LETTER NOV 9 1889'
shows: Outline (meander) of Mound Key island with lot lines and one mound symbol labelled 'Mound'; Estero Bay shoreline with depth-like form lines; section lines/corners. Not a plan of the shell works, but a measured island outline plus mound position.
licence_basis: US federal government work (GLO / US Surveyor General, 1889): public domain
notes: Viewed full plat and high-res crop of lot 4. Island meander is a strong placement aid (coastline + section corner). Earlier 1873 township plat (Survey-15182/15183) does not draw the island.

source_title: GLO original township plat T 19 N - R 10 E, District North of Red River, Louisiana Meridian
author: Aaron Van Dorn, Deputy Surveyor (resurvey under contracts of 1847-48); Surveyor General's Office, Donaldsonville

where.id: BLM GLO Survey-78687; documentID 11855593173498286882; plat accession LA180190N0100E00001

caption_or_quote: Hachured mound symbol labelled 'Indian Mound' just south of the north line of Sec. 14 (line marked 'N 89 35' E 80.'), beside 'Harlin Bayou' where it joins Bayou Macon; notes: 'whole was re-surveyed by Aaron Vandorn Dep: Sur: ... all the balance under contract of February 15th 1848'; 'Surveyor General's Office Donaldsonville La June 19th 18..' (year cut off in the scan)
shows: One mound (symbol + label 'Indian Mound') at the Sec. 11/14 line next to Harlin Bayou, plus Bayou Macon with its bluff hachures, claimant names (Humphries, Grier, Van Rensselaer), section lines with chainages. The mound lies in the site's section (PLSS lookup at the site point = T19N R10E Sec. 14). Which Poverty Point mound it is (B, by Harlin Bayou, is the likely one; A is further SW) is NOT verified - check against LiDAR.
licence_basis: US federal government work (GLO / US Surveyor General, 1848): public domain
notes: Viewed full plat, zoomed sections 11/13/14 at high resolution. Section corners + bayou meander give strong placement control. A 1856 resurvey plat (Survey-78689, John M. Bradford) exists for this township and was not inspected. Approval year is illegible in the scan; the resurvey contract is Feb 1848, so the plat is 1848 or a little later.

source_title: [Map of Harmar and Marietta, Ohio] (with inset 'Ancient Works')
author: C. Sullivan (drawn), P. S. Duval & Co., lithographers, Philadelphia

where.id: LoC G&M 2024593582; IIIF service:gmd:gmd408:g4084:g4084m:ct007598 (8316 x 6305 px)

caption_or_quote: Town plan with the mound drawn as a hachured circle labelled 'Conus' in its own square of the street grid (Sq. 34/35/39 area, next to 'Old Burying Ground'); inset 'ANCIENT WORKS' with Reference 'a. Parapets ... c. Conical mounds ... h. Elevated Square or Capitolum' and the Conus drawn with ring ditch
shows: Conus mound (today Mound Cemetery) located inside the surveyed 1837 town lot/square grid with numbered squares and streets; the Capitolium and Sacra Via also appear in the town plan; inset gives the full earthwork layout (parapets, covert ways, Quadranaou, Capitolium, Conus). Scale of ten chains to one inch.
licence_basis: Published 1837 (pre-1931): public domain in the US; LoC lists no known restrictions for this item (check rights_advisory before publishing)
notes: Viewed full image (IIIF 50%) and crops of the Conus square and the inset. The street-grid plan is a far better placement source than the S&D plate because the squares survive in today's Marietta street pattern. Also applies to site 'marietta' (already has an overlay).

source_title: [Map of Harmar and Marietta, Ohio] (with inset 'Ancient Works')
author: C. Sullivan (drawn), P. S. Duval & Co., lithographers, Philadelphia
caption_or_quote: Inset titled 'ANCIENT WORKS' with Reference: 'a. Parapets, b. Excavations, c. Conical mounds, d. Large Covert way, e. Small Covert way, f. Pond or Reservoir, g. Elevated oblong Squares, h. Elevated Square or Capitolum'; main town plan shows 'Conus', 'Capitolium' and 'Sacra Via' within the street grid
shows: Marietta earthworks both as a schematic inset and as features (Conus, Capitolium, Sacra Via) embedded in the 1837 town plat of numbered squares and streets.
licence_basis: Published 1837 (pre-1931): public domain in the US
notes: Site already has an overlay; listed because the town-plat version gives street-grid control points.

source_title: GLO original township plat, Township No. XIX North, Range No. VIII East, 2nd Meridian (Indiana)
author: B. Bentley, Deputy Surveyor (surveyed 1821)

where.id: BLM GLO Survey-458033 (same township also Survey-458035); see glo_ids.txt for documentID/accession

caption_or_quote: Concentric-circle symbol (ring around a hachured centre) on the line between Sec. 15 and Sec. 16, south of the White River, labelled 'Mound & intrenchment'; title 'Township No. XIX North, Range No. VIII East 2nd Mer. Surveyed by B. Bentley, 1821'
shows: The Great Mound earthwork (central mound in a circular ditch-and-embankment) as a symbol with label, placed on a surveyed section line; also White River meanders, 'Buck's T.' (Indian town) with lodge triangles, section/quarter lines with chainages. Lies in the site's section (PLSS lookup = T19N R8E Sec. 16).
licence_basis: US federal government work (GLO, 1821): public domain
notes: Viewed full plat and high-res zoom. Symbol only (not a measured plan), but placed on a section line 1821 - a good locator. A second hachured symbol near the Sec. 10/11/14/15 corner was not identified. Survey-458035 not inspected separately.

source_title: Earthworks, Portsmouth, Ohio (Pl. IV in G. S. B. Hempstead, 'The origin and destiny of the Mound Builders', Journal of the Anthropological Institute vol. VII)
author: G. S. B. Hempstead (delt., survey 1875); J. P. & W. R. Emslie, lith., London

where.id: Commons File:Portsmouth Earthworks map Hempstead 1878.jpg (2000 x 1324)

caption_or_quote: Title 'EARTHWORKS PORTSMOUTH, OHIO'; margin 'Journ. Anthrop. Inst. Vol. VII, Pl. IV'; on the second terrace NE of the town a double horseshoe figure next to the label 'DITCH', with the parallel walls running SE to the Ohio and across to 'TEMPLE MOUND'
shows: Whole Portsmouth group: town street grid of Portsmouth, Scioto and Ohio rivers, terraces, Hocking Valley Railroad, Old Road to Chillicothe, Ohio & Erie Canal, the Kentucky concentric works, Hunting Ground/Springville works, Unionville circle. The horseshoe figure is drawn but not labelled 'Horseshoe' - identification with today's Mound Park horseshoe is by position (NE of the 1875 town grid, end of the parallel walls).
licence_basis: Published 1878 (pre-1931): public domain; Commons lists 'Public domain'
notes: Viewed full image. Strong placement aids (street grid, railroad, rivers). Commons copy is 2000 px only; a better scan of JAI vol. 7 is likely on Internet Archive/BHL. This is a journal plate, so book agents may also find it.

source_title: Earthworks, Portsmouth, Ohio (Pl. IV in G. S. B. Hempstead, 'The origin and destiny of the Mound Builders', Journal of the Anthropological Institute vol. VII)
author: G. S. B. Hempstead (delt., survey 1875); J. P. & W. R. Emslie, lith., London

where.id: Commons File:Portsmouth Earthworks map Hempstead 1878.jpg; detail crop with modern red labels: File:Portsmouth Earthworks map King & Biggs Hempstead 1878.jpg

caption_or_quote: In Kentucky, east of 'TEMPLE MOUND': circle symbol labelled 'MOUND, DITCH & EMBANKMENT / Mound 6 ft high / Ditch 12 deep / Embankt 3 high'; beside it a hexagon and 'MOUND 18 ft high'
shows: Biggs Site drawn as mound-in-ditch-and-embankment symbol with dimensions, next to the Ohio River shore and the big concentric 'Temple Mound' works (Portsmouth Group A).
notes: Viewed full image and the Commons detail crop. The identification 'Biggs Site' for the 'Mound, ditch & embankment' symbol comes from the Commons uploader's modern red overlay, not from the 1878 plate; the alternative is that Biggs is the concentric 'Temple Mound'. Check by position on LiDAR before use.
